video.title: The Abdominal Corkscrew ft. Carson Branstine

classification.reason: The coach provides an actionable drill at the end of the video where the player takes a wide stance and drives the knee to the elbow to feel abdominal tension.

problem.title_as_question: How do you generate effortless power through the abdominal corkscrew?
problem.definition: Players often try to drive power from the hips independently, which discombobulates the swing and fails to transfer speed into the trunk and arm.

quotes.text: The amount of velocity she's able to generate on this backhand with such a small swing is the reason that Lois Bassan is so rushed
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: her trunk, her shoulder line, her chest, it is twisted back farther than her hips.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: the trunk is moving faster than the hips for pretty much the entire swing.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: a lot of people get the idea of hip drive into their mind and that's amazing except it must be connected to the trunk through that tension in the abdomen.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: If your hips are going by themselves, then your swing is actually getting discombobulated and you're losing that tension corkcrew coil that she's recruiting through the abdomen here.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: biomechanically the hips, the pelvis, it actually moves faster than the trunk for about 25 milliseconds. But you're not going to be able to feel that.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: The way you get that to happen is by learning to feel this tension. Again, look at that stretch.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: I want you to aim for that feeling of tension and power in your abdomen rather than thinking about the timing windows because the timing windows are too small for you to actually feel.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: That shoulder line, that upper part of the trunk really needs to yank itself out and participate in that explosive twist.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: What you want to feel is that coiled low tension position. Everything explodes forward during this part of the swing.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: So the purpose of the hips is to speed up the trunk. And then of course the purpose of the trunk is to speed up the arm.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: That effortless power comes from the hips connecting to the trunk through that tension in the abdomen and then flinging the trunk through.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: Her mastery over the abdominal corkcrew everywhere around the court is the only reason she was able to compete with Arena Sabalanka in that second set.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: That tension is what makes it so that as the hips drive, the trunk comes with it.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: Very important not to overfocus on your hips from a sensory perspective because right away the trunk is going with the hips.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: The amount of stretch you use can vary from shot to shot.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: You can wind up more or less. you can load more or less power into your trunk and hips and make that power control trade-off shot by shot as you see fit.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: You get in a nice wide stance and you drive your knee to the elbow on the side of your body like this.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: this is going to help you feel that tension and you're going to be able to explode faster and harder
quotes.speaker: coach

symptoms.description: The swing becomes disconnected and discombobulated when driving the hips without abdominal connection.
Player fails to feel abdominal tension coiling or stretch in the stomach fascia during the load.

causes.statement: The upper trunk is not twisted back farther than the hips to create an abdominal stretch load.
The player focuses solely on hip drive, letting the hips fire in isolation without trunk connection through the abdomen.
The front shoulder line and upper trunk fail to yank forward and actively participate in the explosive twist.

angles.summary: The hips drive to accelerate the trunk, and the trunk uncoils faster than the hips to sling the arm forward.
Players overfocus on hip-shoulder separation timing windows that are only 25 milliseconds long and impossible to feel consciously.
Players should focus on sensing physical tension and coiling in the abdominal muscles and fascia rather than intellectual timing.
Carson Branstine and Carlos Alcaraz both utilize the abdominal stretch to generate explosive effortless groundstroke speed.

solutions.summary: Focus sensory awareness on feeling abdominal tension and power rather than calculating hip-shoulder timing windows.
Do not overfocus on the hips in isolation; feel the upper chest and trunk firing around with the hips from swing initiation.
Adjust the depth of abdominal corkscrew and load depending on the incoming ball to trade off power versus control shot by shot.
Stand in a wide stance and dynamically drive the knee toward the elbow on the side of the body to recruit abdominal tension and explosive uncoiling.
